blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A Deployment keeps identical Pods running. It comes from the apps/v1 API.
blocks.why: This lesson adds three timers that control how Pods start, roll out, and stop.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a Deployment, from the apps/v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: You use the name to watch its rollout.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A name to find the Deployment
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: timing-app

blocks.title: Two copies and their label
blocks.what: Keep two Pods running, and manage the Pods labelled app: timing.
blocks.why: Two copies make the rollout and shutdown timing easy to watch.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 Deployments must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Two copies of the Pods that carry this label
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: timing-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: timing

blocks.title: Describe the Pods
blocks.what: The template is the blueprint for each Pod. It gives each Pod the label app: timing.
blocks.why: The template labels must match the selector, or Kubernetes rejects the Deployment.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Deployment would have nothing to create, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.comment: The blueprint for each Pod, with the label the selector looks for
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: timing-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: timing
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: timing

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: A busybox container that sleeps for an hour. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: sleep ignores the polite stop signal, which shows how the grace period works.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.comment: The container each Pod runs: it sleeps
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: timing-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: timing
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: timing
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]

blocks.title: Wait before counting it ready
blocks.what: minReadySeconds: a new Pod must stay ready for 10 seconds before it counts as available.
blocks.why: A Pod that crashes soon after starting does not count. The rollout waits instead of moving on.
blocks.ifRemoved: A Pod counts as available the moment it is ready.
blocks.comment: A new Pod must stay ready 10 seconds to count
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: timing-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  minReadySeconds: 10
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: timing
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: timing
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]

blocks.title: Give up on a stuck rollout
blocks.what: progressDeadlineSeconds: if a rollout makes no progress for 60 seconds, it is marked as failed.
blocks.why: You and your tools notice a stuck rollout. Kubernetes reports it but does not roll back by itself.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes waits 600 seconds, the default, before reporting a stuck rollout.
blocks.comment: Report the rollout as failed after 60 seconds without progress
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: timing-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  minReadySeconds: 10
  progressDeadlineSeconds: 60
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: timing
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: timing
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]

blocks.title: Time to shut down
blocks.what: terminationGracePeriodSeconds: a stopping container gets 5 seconds to finish, then it is forced to stop.
blocks.why: Apps use the time to finish requests. The default is 30 seconds.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes waits the default 30 seconds before forcing each container to stop.
blocks.comment: Give each container 5 seconds to stop cleanly
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: timing-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  minReadySeconds: 10
  progressDeadlineSeconds: 60
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: timing
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: timing
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 5
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Deployments are in apps/v1.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A Deployment keeps identical Pods running.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The Deployment’s name. Its Pods get names that start with it.
notes.spec: The desired state of the Deployment, including its timers.
notes.spec.replicas: How many Pods to keep running.
notes.spec.minReadySeconds: Seconds a new Pod must stay ready before it counts as available. The default is 0.
notes.spec.progressDeadlineSeconds: Seconds without progress before the rollout is reported as failed. Must be more than minReadySeconds.
notes.spec.selector: Which Pods this Deployment manages. It cannot change after creation.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels to be managed by this Deployment.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels.app: Match Pods whose app label is timing.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for every Pod this Deployment creates.
notes.spec.template.metadata: Details given to every Pod created from the template.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod gets the label app: timing, so the selector finds it.
notes.spec.template.spec: What each Pod runs. This is the same spec as in a Pod file.
notes.spec.template.spec.terminationGracePerio: Seconds a stopping container gets before it is forced to stop. The default is 30.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].command: Sleep for an hour. sleep ignores the polite stop signal.

tryIt.result: Waits about 10 seconds after the Pods start, then prints successfully rolled out.
Takes about 5 seconds. sleep ignores the stop signal, so Kubernetes waits out the grace period.

check.run: start=$(date +%s); kubectl delete pod -l app=timing >/dev/null; echo "took $(( $(date +%s) - start ))s"

tryIt.result: Removes the Deployment and its Pods.

questions.question: What does minReadySeconds: 10 do?
answers: A new Pod must stay ready 10 seconds before it counts as available
The rollout must finish in 10 seconds
questions.explain: A Pod that crashes soon after starting never counts. The rollout waits for a steady Pod.

questions.question: A rollout makes no progress for 60 seconds. What does Kubernetes do?
answers: Rolls back to the old version
questions.explain: The Deployment gets the ProgressDeadlineExceeded reason. Rolling back is up to you or your tools.

questions.question: An app ignores the stop signal. How long until it is forced to stop?
questions.explain: terminationGracePeriodSeconds is how long Kubernetes waits before forcing the stop.

fix.message: The Deployment "timing-app" is invalid: spec.progressDeadlineSeconds: Invalid value: 5: must be greater than minReadySeconds
fix.explain: The deadline must be longer than minReadySeconds. Otherwise no Pod could count as available in time.
